# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

Security fixes are released for the latest minor version of the current major release line.

| Version | Supported          |
| ------- | ------------------ |
| 1.x     | :white_check_mark: |
| < 1.0   | :x:                |

## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues, discussions, or pull requests.** A public report discloses the issue to everyone, including people who may abuse it, before a fix exists.

Instead, use one of the following private channels:

1. **GitHub private vulnerability reporting** (preferred) — go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/kingmaker-agm/filament-filter-sets/security) of this repository and choose **Report a vulnerability**.
2. **Email** — [pratheep@kingmaker.co.in](mailto:pratheep@kingmaker.co.in), with `SECURITY` in the subject line.

### What to include

The more of the following you can provide, the faster the issue can be confirmed and fixed:

- The version of `kingmaker/filament-filter-sets` affected
- Your Filament, Laravel, and PHP versions
- A description of the vulnerability and the impact you believe it has
- Steps to reproduce, ideally with a minimal code sample
- Any proof-of-concept, log output, or stack trace you have

### What to expect

This is a community-maintained package, so the timelines below are targets rather than guarantees:

- **Acknowledgement** of your report within 5 business days.
- An **assessment** — whether the issue is confirmed, and a rough severity — within 10 business days.
- A **fix released** as a patch version as soon as practical after confirmation, with a GitHub Security Advisory published once the fix is available.

You will be credited in the advisory for the discovery unless you would rather stay anonymous. Please give a reasonable window for a fix to ship before disclosing the issue publicly.

## Scope

This policy covers the code in this repository. Vulnerabilities in the underlying frameworks and libraries should be reported to their own maintainers:

- [Filament](https://github.com/filamentphp/filament/security/policy)
- [Laravel](https://github.com/laravel/framework/security/policy)
- [Livewire](https://github.com/livewire/livewire/security/policy)
